creative.body:
I haven't let my husband touch me in 4 months.

Not really touched me. Not the way he used to. Not the way a 32-year marriage is supposed to feel.

I sleep on the far edge of the bed. I undress in the bathroom with the door closed. I wear my husband's old t-shirts to sleep instead of the nightgowns I bought for myself last spring. I turn the lights off the second I get in. I make a joke when he reaches for me at 11pm, and I roll over.

He has not asked me what's wrong. I think he's afraid of the answer. I am afraid of giving it.

The corner of the bed.

I have measured it. I sleep about 4 inches from the edge of the mattress on my side. I know because I rolled out of bed once at 2am trying to get further away in my sleep and I bruised my hip on the nightstand. I keep an extra pillow lengthwise between us now. I tell him I sleep better with it. What I am actually doing is building a wall the width of a body pillow down the center of a bed we have shared for 32 years. Some nights I lie there with my back to him and I count how many inches of mattress are between his shoulder and mine. The number has gotten bigger every month.

The closed bathroom door.

For 30 years I undressed in our bedroom. I did not think about it. I would come up the stairs after dinner and step out of my clothes wherever I was standing. He would come in from brushing his teeth and we would talk about the day with me half in a robe. That ended in October. Now I take my clothes into the bathroom. I shut the door. I lock it. I undress sitting on the edge of the tub because by 9pm my abdomen is so distended I cannot bend at the waist comfortably. I press my fingers into my stomach and they do not give. I put on his t-shirt. I open the door. I get in the bed in the dark. He is already on his side, pretending to read.

The t-shirts in the drawer.

The top drawer of his dresser has a stack of old gym shirts from a charity 5K he ran in 2014. They are soft from a decade of washing. I have been pulling 1 of them out every night for 4 months. The drawer is half empty now because I keep them on my side. The blue silk nightgown I bought last spring is in the closet, on a hanger, with the original tag still on the strap. There is a pale pink one next to it I have never worn either. I walk past them every morning when I am getting dressed and I do not look at them. I bought them in a store in March before any of this started, in a fitting room where I cried because the size was 2 numbers smaller than what I had worn in 10 years. I had thought they were going to be a gift to him. They have been hanging untouched in our closet for 7 months.

The October wedding.

My niece got married on a Saturday in October at a vineyard 3 hours from our house. I wore a green dress I had bought for the occasion. It was the first dress I had worn in years that did not have an elastic waist. My husband stood next to me at the ceremony with his hand on the small of my back. He kept looking at me. On the drive home, twice, he said, "You looked beautiful tonight." Once on the highway and once when we pulled into our driveway. I went to bed that night thinking we were finally on the other side of something. By Christmas the dress would not button. Not because I had gained weight. I was still losing. The bloating had moved my middle out 2 inches past where my hips were. The dress was cut for a body that narrowed at the waist. My waist was now wider than the bottom of my ribs. I tried it on in the bathroom on Christmas Eve and I could not get the zipper past my stomach. I sat on the closed toilet in the green dress unzipped down the back and I cried so quietly he could not hear me from the bedroom.

The Tuesday night.

He sat down on the edge of the bed before I got in. He had his hands on his knees. He was looking at the floor.

He said, "I need to ask you something. I am not going to ask it again."

I waited.

He said, "Are you thinking about leaving me."

I started crying so hard I could not answer. I sat down on the edge of the bed next to him and I put my hand on his back and I cried into his shoulder for what must have been 10 minutes. He did not say anything else. He just sat there. He let me cry. When I could finally breathe I told him no. I told him no. I told him no. I did not tell him why I had been sleeping in the corner. He did not ask. We got into bed. He stayed on his side. I stayed on mine. I do not think either of us slept.

The wedding 2 weekends later.

It was my younger niece this time. A different vineyard. I wore a navy dress that hid as much of my middle as I could hide. By the time the reception started I had already been bloated for 4 hours. I made it through dinner. I made it through the toasts. I made it through the first dance. When my husband held out his hand to dance with me I told him I needed the bathroom and I almost ran.

I got into the largest stall in the bathroom lounge and I sat on the closed toilet in my dress and I cried so hard I thought I might be sick. I do not know how long I was in there. Long enough that someone knocked. A woman's voice. Calm. Older. She said, "Honey. I am not going to ask. I just want to know if you are alright. I will sit out here until you come out."

I came out 5 minutes later. The woman on the bench in the lounge was 62. Her name was Eleanor. A friend of my mother-in-law's. I had met her maybe 3 times in 30 years. She was alone at the wedding because her husband Tom had died 4 years ago. She did not ask me anything. She handed me a tissue. She patted the bench next to her. I sat down. We sat for maybe 2 minutes in silence. Then I told her. About the Wegovy. About the bloating. About sleeping in his t-shirts. About Tuesday night.

When I was done she was quiet for a long time. Then she said, "I want to tell you something I have not told very many people. I lost my marriage to the same thing 4 years ago. Different cause, same outcome."

She told it to me very slowly. She had a hysterectomy at 53. The constipation started 3 months after. Miralax, magnesium, every product she could find. The bloating was so bad by 4pm she could not bear to be touched. Tom moved into the guest room because she told him she needed space to sleep. She told herself it was temporary. She said the next part barely above a whisper.

He never came back. They lived in the same house for 4 more years like that. He died in that room. They had been married 38 years. She would give anything for one of those 4 years back.

I started crying again. She let me. Then she said the thing I think she had wanted someone to say to her.

"Your medication works in 2 places. Not 1. The brain part is the engine of the weight loss. Do not undo it. The stomach part is where every symptom you have is coming from. Every product on every shelf works 6 feet downstream from the actual problem. Apigenin works on the right organ."

5 sentences. That was all she said about the mechanism. She did not lecture me. She did not draw me a diagram. She held my hand on the bench and she gave me the 5 sentences and she let me sit with them.

She told me the brand name before I left. Motilli. Standardized apigenin extract from celery, not powder. Combined with chlorophyllin and a soluble prebiotic. Heart-shaped gummies, 2 a day. She said she had taken it on her own body 2 years ago because she wanted to know if it would have worked for her and Tom. She said it did. She said she thinks about him every time she takes one.

I sat next to her for another 10 minutes. We did not talk. She held my hand on top of the bench.

I ordered it from the hotel room that night while my husband was in the shower. The package arrived 3 days later.

I read for the next 4 nights to understand what Eleanor had handed me on the bench.

The medication works in 2 places. The first place is the brain. The signal that I am full when I have only eaten half. The reason I have lost 34 pounds and stopped pre-diabetic blood sugar and stopped having to ice my knees after a grocery run. That is the engine of the weight loss. I do not want to undo that part.

The second place is the stomach. The medication takes the stomach from normal to nearly frozen. Food that should leave in 4 hours sits there for 10 or 12. While it sits, bacteria ferment it. Gas builds. Pressure builds. By 4pm my abdomen is bigger than my hips because the food from breakfast and lunch is sitting up there fermenting. The bloating I cannot bear to be touched on top of is happening in my stomach. Not my colon.

Every product my GI handed me works on the colon. Miralax, magnesium, Colace, fiber. All of them. They pull water into a pipe that already has nothing in it because the food is trapped 6 feet upstream. They have been flushing an empty pipe for 7 months while the actual clog sat untouched at the top.

Apigenin works on the smooth muscle of the stomach wall. Not a laxative. Not a stimulant. Does not produce dependency. Does not override the brain part of the medication. Only acts on the stomach side effect. The drug keeps doing its job. The food just stops rotting inside me.

That is what Eleanor figured out 4 years too late.

The week I started Motilli, I slept in the corner of the bed every night. Days 1 through 4, nothing. Day 5 the pressure under my ribs by 4pm was not as sharp. Day 9 I went on my own, no Miralax, no magnesium. Day 14 my husband put his arm around me on the couch after dinner and I did not pull away. The Saturday of week 3 I came out of the bathroom in the blue silk nightgown for the first time. He looked up from his book and did not say anything for a second and then he said, "There she is." I cried in his lap for 20 minutes before he understood why. The Sunday morning of week 4 I moved his old gym t-shirts back into his drawer. The Tuesday night of week 5 I slept in the middle of the bed for the first time in 5 months. He woke up at 3am and put his hand on my hip and I let him. Week 6 he saw the empty bathroom counter and said, "Took you long enough."

I am wearing the blue nightgown right now as I write this. The pale pink one is in the laundry. The Tuesday night when he asked me if I was thinking about leaving him did not end our marriage. It saved it. He asked the question I could not ask myself.

The medication works in 2 places. Brain part is the engine. Stomach part is where every symptom is coming from. Every product on every shelf works 6 feet downstream. Apigenin works on the right organ.

I am not affiliated with the company. Motilli runs a 90-day money-back guarantee. They batch-produce because apigenin degrades from light and heat, so the bottles sell out for stretches. If you have an anniversary, a vacation, a weekend coming up where you want to be in your own body again, I would not wait until next week.

The link is below.

Susan

P.S. Eleanor's husband Tom is buried 4 hours from where I live. I drove there last month. I had to ask the cemetery office where to find him. I laid a small bunch of flowers on his stone and I sat on the grass for a while and I told him thank you. Thank you for letting his wife find me on a bench in a bathroom lounge at somebody else's wedding. Thank you for letting her save mine.
